ordered_diagnoses: Stress fracture of the femoral neck

facts.raw_span: one week of right hip pain
difficulty walking
denosumab for osteoporosis for five years
total hip arthroplasty for a left femoral neck fracture two years earlier
JOA score was 96 on the right and 76 on the left
Initial plain radiographs at an outside clinic were reportedly normal
Repeat radiographs at our hospital demonstrated an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck
Computed tomography confirmed a lateral cortical fracture without comminution
T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a high-signal bend in the same region
Bone mineral density was 0.840 g/cm2 in the lumbar spine and 0.899 g/cm2 in the right femoral neck
calcium 9.7 mg/dL
alkaline phosphatase 47 IU/L

aliases: atypical fracture of the femoral neck
concepts.why: The patient's presentation of right hip pain and difficulty walking, combined with radiographic evidence of an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck, is consistent with an atypical femoral fracture, which is a known complication of long-term denosumab use for osteoporosis.
The patient's history of osteoporosis and low bone mineral density, as well as the presence of a fracture, supports the diagnosis of an osteoporotic fracture.

concepts.preferred_label: Stress fracture of the femoral neck
concepts.why: The patient's presentation of hip pain and radiographic evidence of a fracture in the femoral neck is consistent with a stress fracture, which can occur in the absence of significant trauma.
The patient's long-term use of denosumab for osteoporosis increases the risk of osteonecrosis of the jaw, although there is no direct evidence of this condition in the provided vignette.
The patient's radiographic evidence of a fracture in the femoral neck supports the diagnosis of a femoral neck fracture.
The patient's low bone mineral density is consistent with osteopenia, which is a precursor to osteoporosis.

The patient's presentation of hip pain and radiographic evidence of a fracture in the femoral neck is consistent with an insufficiency fracture, which occurs when a normal stress is applied to a weakened bone.
The patient's history of osteoporosis and low bone mineral density, as well as the presence of a fracture, supports the diagnosis of a bone fragility fracture.

rationales.F03: Denosumab use is a known risk factor for atypical femoral fractures.
rationales.F04: A history of total hip arthroplasty for a femoral neck fracture increases the risk of another femoral neck fracture.
rationales.F07: An incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck is a characteristic finding of atypical femoral fractures.
rationales.F08: Computed tomography confirmation of a lateral cortical fracture without comminution supports the diagnosis of an atypical femoral fracture.
rationales.F09: T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrating a high-signal bend in the same region is consistent with an atypical femoral fracture.
rationales.F10: Low bone mineral density is a risk factor for osteoporotic fractures and bone fragility fractures.
